newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes steadier, but still bearish.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes steadier, but still bearish.

text.p: The tone across the precious metals markets was still bearish on Friday afternoon after gold and platinum dipped to fresh lows stretching back over three years in the morning.
But gold showed some reluctance to fall below $364.00 per ounce as it became slightly oversold, some dealers said.
"The tone is still bearish," one added, while another referred to "gold's bearish internal combustion" as overwhelming any positive influence for the moment.
Bullion was fixed at $364.00 against $364.30 this morning and $366.55 on Thursday afternoon. Friday's fixes were fresh lows since a $363.00 nadir on November 3, 1993.
The Comex futures opened lower as forecast and by the fixing the February contract was pulled back about $1.40 at $365.20.
Dealers noted that the market was still working at half speed after the Christmas and New Year holidays with many dealers not back at their desks yet and Japan closed for a week of national holdays.
"Things are relatively steady today after the fund selling (on Thursday) but it is clear the markets still want to go lower," a dealer said.
He added that any rally based on short covering would be short lived through incoming profit-taking.
Industrial precious metals users were expected to start returning to the market after the holidays next week but that was unlikely to change the outlook.
"Physical buying may slow the fall but the market will not turn round until the speculators begin to buy instead of sell," one dealer said.
However another market source dismissed the seasonal issue saying the current fatigue was just a continuation of bearish feeling that marked December.
Platinum was also steadier than in the morning after posting an afternoon fix 50 cents lower than earlier at $366.00, a fresh low since November 2, 1993.
"There is not much on the upside and Japan being away doesn't help either," said one dealer.
Palladium held gains from fund buying on Nymex on Tuesday.
It was indicated at $120.00/$121.00 just 25 cents down overnight and against $116.50 at Tuesday's London close.
Silver managed a bounce off $4.66 to be indicated at $4.69/$4.71, down five cents.
